content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The IP/data rule is satisfied by the ownership architecture of this transfer and servicing agreement:

- **Section 2.1(a)/(b)** — the Depositor "transfers and absolutely assigns to the Issuer... all of the Depositor's right, title and interest" in the Receivables and related Depositor Transferred Property. Assignment runs *to* our side.
- **Section 9.2** — Depositor may not further transfer, assign or encumber the Depositor Transferred Property, and must defend the Issuer's interest.
- **Section 9.4(a)** — Cellco must mark its own receivables systems to show clearly that each Receivable is owned by the Issuer and pledged to the Indenture Trustee.
- **Section 3.10(b)** — Receivable Files (including the receivables systems on which they are stored) are held in custody "for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee"; **Section 7.5(b)** requires delivery of the Receivable Files and the accounts and records to a Successor Servicer on transition.

Nothing assigns our property, records or obligor data to Cellco, and no joint ownership is created — so no walk-away exposure. The one counterparty-favourable carve-out, Section 7.5(b) ("will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications"), is Cellco retaining its own platform and know-how, which the playbook expressly permits and which sits at the **fallback** position.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: there is no express licence-back of the Servicer's servicing software/systems to support a servicing transition — a sub-element short of the preferred position, not a material fallback failure in a securitisation TSA where no deliverables are procured.
